_meta.source: Written by the indic-linguistics agent (a language model) for task P1-17. Synthetic; not copied from any call, dataset or private fixture. The numbers are made up and identify nothing.
_meta.notes: Cases for ADR 0017: invisible and bidi characters inside native-script text. Free text keeps all of them (verbatim); a label rejects most of them; the bidi flag is set only for U+202A..U+202E and U+2066..U+2069. Every special character is stored as a raw code point, not as a JSON escape (see the README); the line feed is the JSON escape for a newline.

cases.purpose: Left-to-right marks around a made-up number: LRM does not set the bidi flag and display_safe leaves it unchanged.
Right-to-left marks in Devanagari text: RLM does not set the bidi flag.
Right-to-left override inside a made-up account number (the ADR 0017 example): stored verbatim, flag set, display_safe shows [RLO].
Isolate controls U+2066 and U+2069 around a word: flag set, display_safe shows [LRI] and [PDI].
Zero-width space between words: free text keeps it, a label rejects it.
Word joiner U+2060 and byte-order mark U+FEFF inside text: kept verbatim in free text, rejected in a label.
Soft hyphen U+00AD: kept verbatim in free text, rejected in a label (a default-ignorable character).
Variation selector U+FE0F after a word: kept verbatim in free text, rejected in a label.
Line separator U+2028 between words: kept verbatim in free text, rejected in a label.
A line feed inside a turn: kept verbatim in free text (JSON-escaped on output), rejected in a label.
The ADR 0017 account-number example in English: flag set, display_safe shows [RLO].
Joiners are the only invisible characters a label accepts: the legacy chillu word followed by a stray ZWJ + ZWNJ pair stays whole in free text and is accepted as a label.
